<h1 id="exoscale-api-role">role</h1>

IAM roles lets you define logical sets of policies to grant to users and API keys.

<a href="https://community.exoscale.com/product/iam/operation/role-mgmt/">Read more</a>

## [BETA] Request generation of key/secret that allow caller to assume target role

<a id="opIdassume-iam-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/iam-role/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/assume \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ttl": 1
  }'
```

`POST /iam-role/{id}/assume`

[BETA] Request generation of key/secret that allow caller to assume target role

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ttl": 1
}
```

<h3 id="beta-request-generation-of-keysecret-that-allow-caller-to-assume-target-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ttl|body|integer(int64)|true|TTL in seconds for the generated access key (cannot exceed the max TTL defined in the targeted assume role)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "org-id": "string",
  "role-id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "expires-at": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="beta-request-generation-of-keysecret-that-allow-caller-to-assume-target-role-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|200|Inline|

<h3 id="beta-request-generation-of-keysecret-that-allow-caller-to-assume-target-role-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|org-id|string|false|none|none|
|role-id|string|false|none|none|
|secret|string|false|none|none|
|expires-at|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update IAM Role

<a id="opIdupdate-iam-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/iam-role/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "permissions": [
      "bypass-governance-retention"
    ],
    "labels": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "max-session-ttl": 1,
    "assume-role-policy": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "action": "allow",
          "expression": "string",
          "resources": [
            "string"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /iam-role/{id}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "permissions": [
    "bypass-governance-retention"
  ],
  "labels": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "max-session-ttl": 1,
  "assume-role-policy": {
    "rules": [
      {
        "action": "allow",
        "expression": "string",
        "resources": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-iam-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|IAM Role description|
|» permissions|body|[string]|false|IAM Role permissions|
|» labels|body|[labels](#schemalabels)|false|IAM Role labels|
|» max-session-ttl|body|integer(int64)|false|Maximum TTL requester is allowed to ask for when assuming a role|
|» assume-role-policy|body|[iam-assume-role-policy](#schemaiam-assume-role-policy)|false|IAM Assume role policy|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» permissions|bypass-governance-retention|
|» permissions|reset-iam-organization-policy|

```json
  "message": "string",
  "state": "failure"
}
```

```json
            {
```

```bash
        "property2": {

          "rules": [
            {

              "expression": "string",
              "resources": [
                "string"

          ]
        }
      }
```

```bash
    "assume-role-policy": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "action": "allow",
          "expression": "string",
          "resources": [
            "string"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "max-session-ttl": 1
  }'
```

`POST /iam-role`

```json
{

  "editable": true,

      {
        "action": "allow",
```

<h3 id="create-iam-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|IAM Role name|
|» description|body|string|false|IAM Role description|
|» permissions|body|[string]|false|IAM Role permissions|
|» editable|body|boolean|false|Sets if the IAM Role Policy is editable or not (default: true). This setting cannot be changed after creation|
|» labels|body|[labels](#schemalabels)|false|IAM Role labels|
|» policy|body|[iam-policy](#schemaiam-policy)|false|IAM Role policy|
|» assume-role-policy|body|[iam-assume-role-policy](#schemaiam-assume-role-policy)|false|IAM Assume role policy|
|» max-session-ttl|body|integer(int64)|false|Maximum TTL requester is allowed to ask for when assuming a role|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» permissions|bypass-governance-retention|
|» permissions|reset-iam-organization-policy|

## Generate a new Kubeconfig file for a SKS cluster

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/sks-cluster-kubeconfig/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ttl": 1,
    "user": "string",
    "groups": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /sks-cluster-kubeconfig/{id}`

This operation returns a Kubeconfig file encoded in base64.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ttl": 1,
  "user": "string",
  "groups": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» ttl|body|integer(int64)|false|Validity in seconds of the Kubeconfig user certificate (default: 30 days)|
|» user|body|string|true|User name in the generated Kubeconfig. The certificate present in the Kubeconfig will also have this name set for the CN field.|
|» groups|body|[string]|true|List of roles. The certificate present in the Kubeconfig will have these roles set in the Org field.|

```json
  "kubeconfig": "string"
}
```

## Reveal the password used during instance creation or the latest password reset.

<a id="opIdreveal-instance-password"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/instance/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08:password \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /instance/{id}:password`

Reveal the password used during instance creation or the latest password reset.
            This is only available for VMs created against templates having the `password-enabled`
            property set to `true`.

            Passwords are transiently stored for at most 24 hours and intended to be retrieved shortly after
            creation or resets.

## Reset a Compute instance to a base/target template

<a id="opIdreset-instance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/instance/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08:reset \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "template": {
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    },
    "disk-size": 10
  }'
```

`PUT /instance/{id}:reset`

This operation re-installs a Compute instance to a base template. If target template is provided it will be used to recreated instance from. Warning: the operation wipes all data stored on the disk.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "template": {
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  },
  "disk-size": 10
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» template|body|[template-ref](#schematemplate-ref)|false|Template to recreate Instance from|
|» disk-size|body|integer(int64)|false|Instance disk size in GiB|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "reason": "incorrect",
  "reference": {

    "link": "string",

  },
```

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/instance/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08:revert-snapshot \
```

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /instance/{instance-id}:revert-snapshot`

This operation reverts the snapshot to the Compute instance volume, restoring stored data as it was at the time of the snapshot.
The Compute instance must be previously stopped.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

|» settings|body|object|false|none|

```bash
        "comment": "string",
        "tag": "string"
      }
    ],
    "disable-consumer-stats": true,

  }
```
```json
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» settings|body|object|false|none|
|» » datadog-api-key|body|string|true|Datadog API key|
|» » site|body|[enum-datadog-site](#schemaenum-datadog-site)|false|Datadog intake site. Defaults to datadoghq.com|
|» » datadog-tags|body|[[dbaas-datadog-tag](#schemadbaas-datadog-tag)]|false|Custom tags provided by user|
|» » disable-consumer-stats|body|boolean|false|Disable kafka consumer group metrics. Applies only when attached to kafka services.|
|» » kafka-consumer-check-instances|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of separate instances to fetch kafka consumer statistics with. Applies only when attached to kafka services.|
|» » kafka-consumer-stats-timeout|body|integer(int64)|false|Number of seconds that datadog will wait to get consumer statistics from brokers. Applies only when attached to kafka services.|
|» » max-partition-contexts|body|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of partition contexts to send. Applies only when attached to kafka services.|

<h3 id="update-a-dbaas-opensearch-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[dbaas-service-name](#schemadbaas-service-name)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» max-index-count|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum number of indexes to keep before deleting the oldest one|
|» keep-index-refresh-interval|body|boolean|false|Aiven automation resets index.refresh_interval to default value for every index to be sure that indices are always visible to search. If it doesn't fit your case, you can disable this by setting up this flag to true.|
|» ip-filter|body|[string]|false|Allow incoming connections from CIDR address block, e.g. '10.20.0.0/16'|
|» termination-protection|body|boolean|false|Service is protected against termination and powering off|
|» index-patterns|body|[object]|false|Allows you to create glob style patterns and set a max number of indexes matching this pattern you want to keep. Creating indexes exceeding this value will cause the oldest one to get deleted. You could for example create a pattern looking like 'logs.?' and then create index logs.1, logs.2 etc, it will delete logs.1 once you create logs.6. Do note 'logs.?' does not apply to logs.10. Note: Setting max_index_count to 0 will do nothing and the pattern gets ignored.|
|» » max-index-count|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum number of indexes to keep|
|» » sorting-algorithm|body|string|false|Deletion sorting algorithm|
|» » pattern|body|string|false|fnmatch pattern|
|» maintenance|body|object|false|Automatic maintenance settings|
|» » dow|body|string|true|Day of week for installing updates|
|» » time|body|string|true|Time for installing updates, UTC|
|» index-template|body|object|false|Template settings for all new indexes|
|» » mapping-nested-objects-limit|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|The maximum number of nested JSON objects that a single document can contain across all nested types. This limit helps to prevent out of memory errors when a document contains too many nested objects. Default is 10000.|
|» » number-of-replicas|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|The number of replicas each primary shard has.|
|» » number-of-shards|body|integer(int64)|false|The number of primary shards that an index should have.|
|» opensearch-settings|body|[json-schema-opensearch](#schemajson-schema-opensearch)|false|OpenSearch-specific settings|
|» version|body|string|false|Version|
|» plan|body|string|false|Subscription plan|
|» opensearch-dashboards|body|object|false|OpenSearch Dashboards settings|
|» » opensearch-request-timeout|body|integer(int64)|false|Timeout in milliseconds for requests made by OpenSearch Dashboards towards OpenSearch (default: 30000)|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable or disable OpenSearch Dashboards (default: true)|
|» » max-old-space-size|body|integer(int64)|false|Limits the maximum amount of memory (in MiB) the OpenSearch Dashboards process can use. This sets the max_old_space_size option of the nodejs running the OpenSearch Dashboards. Note: the memory reserved by OpenSearch Dashboards is not available for OpenSearch. (default: 128)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » sorting-algorithm|alphabetical|
|» » sorting-algorithm|creation_date|
|» » dow|saturday|
|» » dow|tuesday|
|» » dow|never|
|» » dow|wednesday|
|» » dow|sunday|
|» » dow|friday|
|» » dow|monday|
|» » dow|thursday|

```json
    "action_auto_create_index_enabled": false,
    "http_max_content_length": 1,
    "thread_pool_write_size": 1,
    "thread_pool_search_queue_size": 10,
    "knn_memory_circuit_breaker_limit": 50,
    "indices_query_bool_max_clause_count": 64,
    "thread_pool_search_throttled_queue_size": 10,
    "cluster_max_shards_per_node": 1000
  },
  "version": "string",
  "recovery-backup-name": "string",
  "plan": "string",
  "opensearch-dashboards": {
    "opensearch-request-timeout": 5000,
    "enabled": true,
    "max-old-space-size": 64
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-dbaas-opensearch-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|[dbaas-service-name](#schemadbaas-service-name)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» max-index-count|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum number of indexes to keep before deleting the oldest one|
|» keep-index-refresh-interval|body|boolean|false|Aiven automation resets index.refresh_interval to default value for every index to be sure that indices are always visible to search. If it doesn't fit your case, you can disable this by setting up this flag to true.|
|» ip-filter|body|[string]|false|Allow incoming connections from CIDR address block, e.g. '10.20.0.0/16'|
|» termination-protection|body|boolean|false|Service is protected against termination and powering off|
|» fork-from-service|body|[dbaas-service-name](#schemadbaas-service-name)|false|Service to fork from|
|» index-patterns|body|[object]|false|Allows you to create glob style patterns and set a max number of indexes matching this pattern you want to keep. Creating indexes exceeding this value will cause the oldest one to get deleted. You could for example create a pattern looking like 'logs.?' and then create index logs.1, logs.2 etc, it will delete logs.1 once you create logs.6. Do note 'logs.?' does not apply to logs.10. Note: Setting max_index_count to 0 will do nothing and the pattern gets ignored.|
|» » max-index-count|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum number of indexes to keep|
|» » sorting-algorithm|body|string|false|Deletion sorting algorithm|
|» » pattern|body|string|false|fnmatch pattern|
|» maintenance|body|object|false|Automatic maintenance settings|
|» » dow|body|string|true|Day of week for installing updates|
|» » time|body|string|true|Time for installing updates, UTC|
|» index-template|body|object|false|Template settings for all new indexes|
|» » mapping-nested-objects-limit|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|The maximum number of nested JSON objects that a single document can contain across all nested types. This limit helps to prevent out of memory errors when a document contains too many nested objects. Default is 10000.|
|» » number-of-replicas|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|The number of replicas each primary shard has.|
|» » number-of-shards|body|integer(int64)|false|The number of primary shards that an index should have.|
|» opensearch-settings|body|[json-schema-opensearch](#schemajson-schema-opensearch)|false|OpenSearch-specific settings|
|» version|body|string|false|OpenSearch major version|
|» recovery-backup-name|body|string|false|Name of a backup to recover from for services that support backup names|
|» plan|body|string|true|Subscription plan|
|» opensearch-dashboards|body|object|false|OpenSearch Dashboards settings|
|» » opensearch-request-timeout|body|integer(int64)|false|Timeout in milliseconds for requests made by OpenSearch Dashboards towards OpenSearch (default: 30000)|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable or disable OpenSearch Dashboards (default: true)|
|» » max-old-space-size|body|integer(int64)|false|Limits the maximum amount of memory (in MiB) the OpenSearch Dashboards process can use. This sets the max_old_space_size option of the nodejs running the OpenSearch Dashboards. Note: the memory reserved by OpenSearch Dashboards is not available for OpenSearch. (default: 128)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » sorting-algorithm|alphabetical|
|» » sorting-algorithm|creation_date|
|» » dow|saturday|
|» » dow|tuesday|
|» » dow|never|
|» » dow|wednesday|
|» » dow|sunday|
|» » dow|friday|
|» » dow|monday|
|» » dow|thursday|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|name|path|[dbaas-service-name](#schemadbaas-service-name)|true|none|

|» » time|body|string|true|Time for installing updates, UTC|
|» version|body|string|false|Version|
|» plan|body|string|false|Subscription plan|

|» size|body|integer(int64)|false|Template size|

<h1 id="exoscale-api-network-load-balancer">network-load-balancer</h1>

A Network Load Balancer (NLB) is a Layer 4 (TCP/UDP)
                   load balancer that distributes incoming traffic to Compute
                   instances managed by an Instance Pool.

<a href="https://community.exoscale.com/documentation/compute/network-load-balancer/">Read more</a>

## Disable Key Rotation

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/kms-key/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/disable-key-rotation \

```

`POST /kms-key/{id}/disable-key-rotation`

Disable the periodic rotation of a KMS Key.

<h3 id="disable-key-rotation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "rotation": {
    "manual-count": 0,
    "automatic": true,
    "rotation-period": 0,
    "next-at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 100,
  "detail": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="disable-key-rotation-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Key rotation disabled|[disable-kms-key-rotation-response](#schemadisable-kms-key-rotation-response)|
|400|Bad Request|### Errors<br><br>Invalid Origin: The request was rejected because automatic key rotation can only be enabled on a KMS key with origin "exoscale-kms".<br><br>Key Not Found: The request was rejected because the specified KMS Key could not be found.<br><br>Not on Default: The request was rejected because the operation is not allowed on the default key.<br><br>Not on Replica: The request was rejectde because the operation is not allowed on a replica.<br><br>Key is Pending Deletion: The request was rejected because it was performed on a key that is pending deletion.<br><br>Key is Disabled: The request was rejected because the specified KMS key is disabled.<br><br>Invalid Usage: The request was rejected because the operation is only allowed on symmetric keys with usage "encrypt-decrypt".<br><br>Conflict: The request was rejected because the automatic rotation is already enabled for this KMS Key.<br>|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`PUT /instance-pool/{id}:evict`

This operation evicts the specified Compute instances member from the Instance Pool, shrinking it to `&lt;current pool size&gt; - &lt;# evicted members&gt;`.

## List Security Groups.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/security-group \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /security-group`

Lists security groups. When visibility is set to public, lists public security groups.
Public security groups are objects maintained by Exoscale which contain source addresses for
relevant services hosted by Exoscale. They can be used a source in ingress rules and as a destination
in egress rules.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|visibility|private|
|visibility|public|

```json
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "external-sources": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="exoscale-api-event">event</h1>

Events form the basis of the Exoscale audit-trail, a mechanism
                   to query past events performing mutations on resources
                   which happened on an organization.

<a href="https://community.exoscale.com/platform/audit-trail/">Read more</a>

## List Events

<a id="opIdlist-events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/event \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /event`

Retrieve Mutation Events for a given date range. Defaults to retrieving Events for the past 24 hours.
         Both a `from` and `to` arguments can be specified to filter Events over a specific period.
         Events will be the the most descriptive possible but not all fields are mandatory

|---|---|

<h1 id="exoscale-api-crypto">crypto</h1>

A suite of cryptographic primitives offered by the Exoscale KMS.

<a href="https://community.exoscale.com/documentation/security/kms/overview">Read more</a>

## Decrypt

<a id="opIddecrypt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/kms-key/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/decrypt \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encryption-context": "string",
    "ciphertext": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /kms-key/{id}/decrypt`

Decrypts a ciphertext.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encryption-context": "string",
  "ciphertext": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="decrypt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[decrypt-request](#schemadecrypt-request)|true|none|
|» encryption-context|body|string(byte) \| null|false|The exact Base64-encoded Additional Authenticated Data (AAD) used during encryption to verify data integrity.|
|» ciphertext|body|string(byte)|true|The Base64-encoded ciphertext payload to be decrypted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "plaintext": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 100,
  "detail": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="decrypt-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Base64 encoded plaintext.|[decrypt-response](#schemadecrypt-response)|
|400|Bad Request|### Errors<br><br>Key Not Found: The request was rejected because the specified KMS Key could not be found.<br><br>Key is Disabled: The request was rejected because the specified KMS key is disabled.<br><br>Invalid Usage: The request was rejected because the operation is only allowed on symmetric keys with usage "encrypt-decrypt".<br>|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Re-encrypt

<a id="opIdre-encrypt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/kms-key/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/re-encrypt \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "source": {
      "key": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "encryption-context": "string",
      "ciphertext": "string"
    },
    "destination": {
      "key": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "encryption-context": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /kms-key/{id}/re-encrypt`

Decrypts an existing ciphertext using its original key material and re-encrypts the underlying plaintext using a specified KMS key or the latest key material of the same KMS Key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "source": {
    "key": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "encryption-context": "string",
    "ciphertext": "string"
  },
  "destination": {
    "key": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "encryption-context": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="re-encrypt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[re-encrypt-request](#schemare-encrypt-request)|true|none|
|» source|body|object|true|none|
|» » key|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the source key currently protecting the data payload.|
|» » encryption-context|body|string(byte) \| null|false|Optional Base64-encoded encryption context originally appended to the AAD to confirm package validation rules.|
|» » ciphertext|body|string(byte)|true|The Base64-encoded encrypted payload package ready to undergo source-side key decryption.|
|» destination|body|object|true|none|
|» » key|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the target key chosen to encapsulate the newly shifted data translation.|
|» » encryption-context|body|string(byte) \| null|false|Optional new Base64-encoded encryption context to apply under the target destination envelope.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "ciphertext": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 100,
  "detail": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="re-encrypt-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Base64 encoded ciphertext|[re-encrypt-response](#schemare-encrypt-response)|
|400|Bad Request|### Errors<br><br>Key Not Found: The request was rejected because the specified KMS Key could not be found.<br><br>Key is Disabled: The request was rejected because the specified KMS key is disabled.<br><br>Not on Default: The request was rejected because the operation is not allowed on the default key.<br><br>Bad Request: The request was rejected because of an invalid request body or path parameter.<br>|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`PUT /sks-cluster/{id}/nodepool/{sks-nodepool-id}:evict`

```json
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
```

## Create Model

<a id="opIdcreate-model"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api-ch-gva-2.exoscale.com/v2/ai/model \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "huggingface-token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /ai/model`

Model files will be downloaded from Huggingface.

Name must be the exact name of the model on huggingface (ex: openai/gpt-oss-120b or ggml-org/gpt-oss-120b-GGUF).

If the model is under a license then you must provide a Huggingface access token for an account that signed the license agreement

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "huggingface-token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-model-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create-model-request](#schemacreate-model-request)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Model name|
|» huggingface-token|body|string|false|Huggingface Token|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",

    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "link": "string",
    "command": "string"
  },
  "message": "string",
  "state": "failure"
}
```

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 100,
  "detail": "string"
}
```

```json
  "name": "string",
```

```json
    {
```

```json
      "min": 0,

    }
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

### Properties

|leader_eligibility|boolean|false|none|If true, Karapace / Schema Registry on the service nodes can participate in leader election. It might be needed to disable this when the schemas topic is replicated to a secondary cluster and Karapace / Schema Registry there must not participate in leader election. Defaults to `true`.|
|topic_name|string|false|none|The durable single partition topic that acts as the durable log for the data. This topic must be compacted to avoid losing data due to retention policy. Please note that changing this configuration in an existing Schema Registry / Karapace setup leads to previous schemas being inaccessible, data encoded with them potentially unreadable and schema ID sequence put out of order. It's only possible to do the switch while Schema Registry / Karapace is disabled. Defaults to `_schemas`.|

<h2 id="tocS_json-schema-kafka-connect">json-schema-kafka-connect</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajson-schema-kafka-connect"></a>
<a id="schema_json-schema-kafka-connect"></a>
<a id="tocSjson-schema-kafka-connect"></a>
<a id="tocsjson-schema-kafka-connect"></a>

```json
{
  "producer_buffer_memory": 8388608,
  "consumer_max_poll_interval_ms": 300000,
  "producer_compression_type": "gzip",
  "connector_client_config_override_policy": "None",
  "offset_flush_interval_ms": 60000,
  "scheduled_rebalance_max_delay_ms": 300000,
  "consumer_fetch_max_bytes": 52428800,
  "consumer_max_partition_fetch_bytes": 1048576,
  "offset_flush_timeout_ms": 5000,
  "consumer_auto_offset_reset": "earliest",
  "producer_max_request_size": 1048576,
  "producer_batch_size": 1024,
  "session_timeout_ms": 10000,
  "producer_linger_ms": 100,
  "consumer_isolation_level": "read_uncommitted",
  "consumer_max_poll_records": 500
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|producer_buffer_memory|integer|false|none|The total bytes of memory the producer can use to buffer records waiting to be sent to the broker (defaults to 33554432).|
|consumer_max_poll_interval_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum delay in milliseconds between invocations of poll() when using consumer group management (defaults to 300000).|
|producer_compression_type|string|false|none|Specify the default compression type for producers. This configuration accepts the standard compression codecs ('gzip', 'snappy', 'lz4', 'zstd'). It additionally accepts 'none' which is the default and equivalent to no compression.|
|connector_client_config_override_policy|string|false|none|Defines what client configurations can be overridden by the connector. Default is None|
|offset_flush_interval_ms|integer|false|none|The interval at which to try committing offsets for tasks (defaults to 60000).|
|scheduled_rebalance_max_delay_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum delay that is scheduled in order to wait for the return of one or more departed workers before rebalancing and reassigning their connectors and tasks to the group. During this period the connectors and tasks of the departed workers remain unassigned. Defaults to 5 minutes.|
|consumer_fetch_max_bytes|integer|false|none|Records are fetched in batches by the consumer, and if the first record batch in the first non-empty partition of the fetch is larger than this value, the record batch will still be returned to ensure that the consumer can make progress. As such, this is not a absolute maximum.|
|consumer_max_partition_fetch_bytes|integer|false|none|Records are fetched in batches by the consumer.If the first record batch in the first non-empty partition of the fetch is larger than this limit, the batch will still be returned to ensure that the consumer can make progress. |
|offset_flush_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|Maximum number of milliseconds to wait for records to flush and partition offset data to be committed to offset storage before cancelling the process and restoring the offset data to be committed in a future attempt (defaults to 5000).|
|consumer_auto_offset_reset|string|false|none|What to do when there is no initial offset in Kafka or if the current offset does not exist any more on the server. Default is earliest|
|producer_max_request_size|integer|false|none|This setting will limit the number of record batches the producer will send in a single request to avoid sending huge requests.|
|producer_batch_size|integer|false|none|This setting gives the upper bound of the batch size to be sent. If there are fewer than this many bytes accumulated for this partition, the producer will 'linger' for the linger.ms time waiting for more records to show up. A batch size of zero will disable batching entirely (defaults to 16384).|
|session_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|The timeout in milliseconds used to detect failures when using Kafka’s group management facilities (defaults to 10000).|
|producer_linger_ms|integer|false|none|This setting gives the upper bound on the delay for batching: once there is batch.size worth of records for a partition it will be sent immediately regardless of this setting, however if there are fewer than this many bytes accumulated for this partition the producer will 'linger' for the specified time waiting for more records to show up. Defaults to 0.|
|consumer_isolation_level|string|false|none|Transaction read isolation level. read_uncommitted is the default, but read_committed can be used if consume-exactly-once behavior is desired.|
|consumer_max_poll_records|integer|false|none|The maximum number of records returned in a single call to poll() (defaults to 500).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|producer_compression_type|gzip|
|producer_compression_type|snappy|
|producer_compression_type|lz4|
|producer_compression_type|zstd|
|producer_compression_type|none|
|connector_client_config_override_policy|None|
|connector_client_config_override_policy|All|
|consumer_auto_offset_reset|earliest|
|consumer_auto_offset_reset|latest|
|consumer_isolation_level|read_uncommitted|
|consumer_isolation_level|read_committed|

<h2 id="tocS_json-schema-pgaudit">json-schema-pgaudit</h2>

```json
{
  "role": "string",
  "log_parameter": false,
  "log_rows": false,
  "log_level": "log",
  "log_relation": false,
  "log_statement_once": false,
  "log_max_string_length": -1,
  "log_catalog": true,
  "log_nested_statements": true,
  "log_statement": true,
  "log_client": false,
  "feature_enabled": false,
  "log": [
    "all"
  ],
  "log_parameter_max_size": 0
}
```

System-wide settings for the pgaudit extension.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|string|false|none|Specifies the master role to use for object audit logging.|
|log_parameter|boolean|false|none|Specifies that audit logging should include the parameters that were passed with the statement.|
|log_rows|boolean|false|none|none|
|log_level|string|false|none|Specifies the log level that will be used for log entries.|
|log_relation|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether session audit logging should create a separate log entry<br>for each relation (TABLE, VIEW, etc.) referenced in a SELECT or DML statement.|
|log_statement_once|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters with<br>the first log entry for a statement/substatement combination or with every entry.|
|log_max_string_length|integer|false|none|Crop parameters representation and whole statements if they exceed this threshold.<br>A (default) value of -1 disable the truncation.|
|log_catalog|boolean|false|none|Specifies that session logging should be enabled in the case where all relations<br>in a statement are in pg_catalog.|
|log_nested_statements|boolean|false|none|This GUC allows to turn off logging nested statements, that is, statements that are<br>executed as part of another ExecutorRun.|
|log_statement|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters (if enabled).|
|log_client|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether log messages will be visible to a client process such as psql.|
|feature_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable pgaudit extension. When enabled, pgaudit extension will be automatically installed.Otherwise, extension will be uninstalled but auditing configurations will be preserved.|
|log|[string]|false|none|Specifies which classes of statements will be logged by session audit logging.|
|log_parameter_max_size|integer|false|none|Specifies that parameter values longer than this setting (in bytes) should not be logged,<br>but replaced with <long param suppressed>.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|log_level|debug1|
|log_level|debug2|
|log_level|debug3|
|log_level|debug4|
|log_level|debug5|
|log_level|info|
|log_level|notice|
|log_level|warning|
|log_level|log|
|log|all|
|log|ddl|
|log|function|
|log|misc|
|log|misc_set|
|log|read|
|log|role|
|log|write|

<h2 id="tocS_json-schema-kafka">json-schema-kafka</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajson-schema-kafka"></a>
<a id="schema_json-schema-kafka"></a>
<a id="tocSjson-schema-kafka"></a>
<a id="tocsjson-schema-kafka"></a>

```json
{
  "sasl_oauthbearer_expected_audience": "string",
  "group_max_session_timeout_ms": 1800000,
  "log_flush_interval_messages": 9223372036854776000,
  "sasl_oauthbearer_jwks_endpoint_url": "string",
  "max_connections_per_ip": 256,
  "sasl_oauthbearer_expected_issuer": "string",
  "log_index_size_max_bytes": 10485760,
  "auto_create_topics_enable": true,
  "log_index_interval_bytes": 4096,
  "replica_fetch_max_bytes": 1048576,
  "num_partitions": 1,
  "transaction_state_log_segment_bytes": 104857600,
  "replica_fetch_response_max_bytes": 10485760,
  "log_message_timestamp_type": "CreateTime",
  "connections_max_idle_ms": 540000,
  "log_flush_interval_ms": 0,
  "log_preallocate": false,
  "log_segment_delete_delay_ms": 60000,
  "message_max_bytes": 1048588,
  "group_initial_rebalance_delay_ms": 3000,
  "log_local_retention_bytes": -2,
  "log_roll_jitter_ms": 0,
  "transaction_remove_expired_transaction_cleanup_interval_ms": 3600000,
  "transaction_partition_verification_enable": true,
  "default_replication_factor": 1,
  "log_roll_ms": 1,
  "producer_purgatory_purge_interval_requests": 10,
  "log_retention_bytes": -1,
  "min_insync_replicas": 1,
  "compression_type": "gzip",
  "log_message_timestamp_difference_max_ms": 0,
  "log_local_retention_ms": -2,
  "log_message_downconversion_enable": true,
  "sasl_oauthbearer_sub_claim_name": "string",
  "max_incremental_fetch_session_cache_slots": 1000,
  "log_retention_hours": -1,
  "group_min_session_timeout_ms": 6000,
  "socket_request_max_bytes": 10485760,
  "log_segment_bytes": 10485760,
  "log-cleanup-and-compaction": {
    "log_cleaner_delete_retention_ms": 86400000,
    "log_cleaner_max_compaction_lag_ms": 30000,
    "log_cleaner_min_cleanable_ratio": 0.5,
    "log_cleaner_min_compaction_lag_ms": 0,
    "log_cleanup_policy": "delete"
  },
  "offsets_retention_minutes": 10080,
  "log_retention_ms": -1
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sasl_oauthbearer_expected_audience|string|false|none|The (optional) comma-delimited setting for the broker to use to verify that the JWT was issued for one of the expected audiences.|
|group_max_session_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum allowed session timeout for registered consumers. Longer timeouts give consumers more time to process messages in between heartbeats at the cost of a longer time to detect failures.|
|log_flush_interval_messages|integer|false|none|The number of messages accumulated on a log partition before messages are flushed to disk|
|sasl_oauthbearer_jwks_endpoint_url|string|false|none|OIDC JWKS endpoint URL. By setting this the SASL SSL OAuth2/OIDC authentication is enabled. See also other options for SASL OAuth2/OIDC. |
|max_connections_per_ip|integer|false|none|The maximum number of connections allowed from each ip address (defaults to 2147483647).|
|sasl_oauthbearer_expected_issuer|string|false|none|Optional setting for the broker to use to verify that the JWT was created by the expected issuer.|
|log_index_size_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size in bytes of the offset index|
|auto_create_topics_enable|boolean|false|none|Enable auto creation of topics|
|log_index_interval_bytes|integer|false|none|The interval with which Kafka adds an entry to the offset index|
|replica_fetch_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The number of bytes of messages to attempt to fetch for each partition (defaults to 1048576). This is not an absolute maximum, if the first record batch in the first non-empty partition of the fetch is larger than this value, the record batch will still be returned to ensure that progress can be made.|
|num_partitions|integer|false|none|Number of partitions for autocreated topics|
|transaction_state_log_segment_bytes|integer|false|none|The transaction topic segment bytes should be kept relatively small in order to facilitate faster log compaction and cache loads (defaults to 104857600 (100 mebibytes)).|
|replica_fetch_response_max_bytes|integer|false|none|Maximum bytes expected for the entire fetch response (defaults to 10485760). Records are fetched in batches, and if the first record batch in the first non-empty partition of the fetch is larger than this value, the record batch will still be returned to ensure that progress can be made. As such, this is not an absolute maximum.|
|log_message_timestamp_type|string|false|none|Define whether the timestamp in the message is message create time or log append time.|
|connections_max_idle_ms|integer|false|none|Idle connections timeout: the server socket processor threads close the connections that idle for longer than this.|
|log_flush_interval_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum time in ms that a message in any topic is kept in memory before flushed to disk. If not set, the value in log.flush.scheduler.interval.ms is used|
|log_preallocate|boolean|false|none|Should pre allocate file when create new segment?|
|log_segment_delete_delay_ms|integer|false|none|The amount of time to wait before deleting a file from the filesystem|
|message_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size of message that the server can receive.|
|group_initial_rebalance_delay_ms|integer|false|none|The amount of time, in milliseconds, the group coordinator will wait for more consumers to join a new group before performing the first rebalance. A longer delay means potentially fewer rebalances, but increases the time until processing begins. The default value for this is 3 seconds. During development and testing it might be desirable to set this to 0 in order to not delay test execution time.|
|log_local_retention_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size of local log segments that can grow for a partition before it gets eligible for deletion. If set to -2, the value of log.retention.bytes is used. The effective value should always be less than or equal to log.retention.bytes value.|
|log_roll_jitter_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum jitter to subtract from logRollTimeMillis (in milliseconds). If not set, the value in log.roll.jitter.hours is used|
|transaction_remove_expired_transaction_cleanup_interval_ms|integer|false|none|The interval at which to remove transactions that have expired due to transactional.id.expiration.ms passing (defaults to 3600000 (1 hour)).|
|transaction_partition_verification_enable|boolean|false|none|Enable verification that checks that the partition has been added to the transaction before writing transactional records to the partition|
|default_replication_factor|integer|false|none|Replication factor for autocreated topics|
|log_roll_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum time before a new log segment is rolled out (in milliseconds).|
|producer_purgatory_purge_interval_requests|integer|false|none|The purge interval (in number of requests) of the producer request purgatory(defaults to 1000).|
|log_retention_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size of the log before deleting messages|
|min_insync_replicas|integer|false|none|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), min.insync.replicas specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful.|
|compression_type|string|false|none|Specify the final compression type for a given topic. This configuration accepts the standard compression codecs ('gzip', 'snappy', 'lz4', 'zstd'). It additionally accepts 'uncompressed' which is equivalent to no compression; and 'producer' which means retain the original compression codec set by the producer.|
|log_message_timestamp_difference_max_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message|
|log_local_retention_ms|integer|false|none|The number of milliseconds to keep the local log segments before it gets eligible for deletion. If set to -2, the value of log.retention.ms is used. The effective value should always be less than or equal to log.retention.ms value.|
|log_message_downconversion_enable|boolean|false|none|This configuration controls whether down-conversion of message formats is enabled to satisfy consume requests. |
|sasl_oauthbearer_sub_claim_name|string|false|none|Name of the scope from which to extract the subject claim from the JWT. Defaults to sub.|
|max_incremental_fetch_session_cache_slots|integer|false|none|The maximum number of incremental fetch sessions that the broker will maintain.|
|log_retention_hours|integer|false|none|The number of hours to keep a log file before deleting it|
|group_min_session_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|The minimum allowed session timeout for registered consumers. Longer timeouts give consumers more time to process messages in between heartbeats at the cost of a longer time to detect failures.|
|socket_request_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum number of bytes in a socket request (defaults to 104857600).|
|log_segment_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size of a single log file|
|log-cleanup-and-compaction|object|false|none|none|
|offsets_retention_minutes|integer|false|none|Log retention window in minutes for offsets topic|
|log_retention_ms|integer|false|none|The number of milliseconds to keep a log file before deleting it (in milliseconds), If not set, the value in log.retention.minutes is used. If set to -1, no time limit is applied.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|log_message_timestamp_type|CreateTime|
|log_message_timestamp_type|LogAppendTime|
|compression_type|gzip|
|compression_type|snappy|
|compression_type|lz4|
|compression_type|zstd|
|compression_type|uncompressed|
|compression_type|producer|

```json
  },

```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|track_activity_query_size|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of bytes reserved to track the currently executing command for each active session. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|timezone|string|false|none|PostgreSQL service timezone|
|track_io_timing|string|false|none|Enables timing of database I/O calls. The default is `off`. When on, it will repeatedly query the operating system for the current time, which may cause significant overhead on some platforms.|
|pg_stat_monitor.pgsm_enable_query_plan|boolean|false|none|Enables or disables query plan monitoring. Changing this parameter causes a service restart. Only available for PostgreSQL 13+.|
|max_files_per_process|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum number of files that can be open per process. The default is `1000` (upstream default). Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|pg_stat_monitor.pgsm_max_buckets|integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of buckets. Changing this parameter causes a service restart. Only available for PostgreSQL 13+.|
|io_max_concurrency|integer|false|none|EXPERIMENTAL: Controls the maximum number of I/O operations that one process can execute simultaneously. Version 18 and up only. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|wal|object|false|none|none|
|default_toast_compression|string|false|none|Specifies the default TOAST compression method for values of compressible columns. The default is `lz4`. Only available for PostgreSQL 14+.|
|deadlock_timeout|integer|false|none|This is the amount of time, in milliseconds, to wait on a lock before checking to see if there is a deadlock condition. The default is `1000` (upstream default).|
|idle_in_transaction_session_timeout|integer|false|none|Time out sessions with open transactions after this number of milliseconds|
|max_pred_locks_per_transaction|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum predicate locks per transaction. The default is `64` (upstream default). Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|max_replication_slots|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum replication slots. The default is `20`. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|max_sync_workers_per_subscription|integer|false|none|Maximum number of synchronization workers per subscription. The default is `2`.|
|autovacuum|object|false|none|none|
|max_parallel_workers_per_gather|integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of workers that can be started by a single Gather or Gather Merge node. The default is `2` (upstream default).|
|io_combine_limit|integer|false|none|EXPERIMENTAL: Controls the largest I/O size in operations that combine I/O in 8kB units. Version 17 and up only.|
|password_encryption|string \| null|false|none|Chooses the algorithm for encrypting passwords.|
|io_workers|integer|false|none|EXPERIMENTAL: Number of IO worker processes, for io_method=worker. Version 18 and up only. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|pg_partman_bgw.interval|integer|false|none|Sets the time interval in seconds to run pg_partman's scheduled tasks. The default is `3600`.|
|log_line_prefix|string|false|none|Choose from one of the available log formats.|
|log_temp_files|integer|false|none|Log statements for each temporary file created larger than this number of kilobytes, -1 disables|
|max_locks_per_transaction|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum locks per transaction. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|track_commit_timestamp|string|false|none|Record commit time of transactions. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|track_functions|string|false|none|Enables tracking of function call counts and time used.|
|io_max_combine_limit|integer|false|none|EXPERIMENTAL: Controls the largest I/O size in operations that combine I/O in 8kB units, and silently limits the user-settable parameter io_combine_limit. Version 18 and up only. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|io_method|string|false|none|EXPERIMENTAL: Controls the maximum number of I/O operations that one process can execute simultaneously. Version 18 and up only. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|max_stack_depth|integer|false|none|Maximum depth of the stack in bytes. The default is `2097152` (upstream default).|
|max_parallel_workers|integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of workers that the system can support for parallel queries. The default is `8` (upstream default).|
|pg_partman_bgw.role|string|false|none|Controls which role to use for pg_partman's scheduled background tasks.|
|max_logical_replication_workers|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum logical replication workers (taken from the pool of max_parallel_workers). The default is `4` (upstream default). Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|max_prepared_transactions|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum prepared transactions. The default is `0`. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|max_worker_processes|integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of background processes that the system can support. The default is `8`. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|pg_stat_statements.track|string|false|none|Controls which statements are counted. Specify top to track top-level statements (those issued directly by clients), all to also track nested statements (such as statements invoked within functions), or none to disable statement statistics collection. The default is `top`.|
|temp_file_limit|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL temporary file limit in KiB, -1 for unlimited|
|log_error_verbosity|string|false|none|Controls the amount of detail written in the server log for each message that is logged.|
|log_min_duration_statement|integer|false|none|Log statements that take more than this number of milliseconds to run, -1 disables|
|max_standby_streaming_delay|integer|false|none|Max standby streaming delay in milliseconds. The default is `30000` (upstream default).|
|jit|boolean|false|none|Controls system-wide use of Just-in-Time Compilation (JIT).|
|max_standby_archive_delay|integer|false|none|Max standby archive delay in milliseconds. The default is `30000` (upstream default).|
|bg-writer|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_json-schema-mysql">json-schema-mysql</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajson-schema-mysql"></a>
<a id="schema_json-schema-mysql"></a>
<a id="tocSjson-schema-mysql"></a>
<a id="tocsjson-schema-mysql"></a>

```json
{
  "net_write_timeout": 30,
  "internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine": "TempTable",
  "sql_mode": "ANSI,TRADITIONAL",
  "information_schema_stats_expiry": 86400,
  "sort_buffer_size": 262144,
  "innodb_thread_concurrency": 10,
  "innodb_write_io_threads": 10,
  "innodb_ft_min_token_size": 3,
  "innodb_change_buffer_max_size": 30,
  "innodb_flush_neighbors": 0,
  "tmp_table_size": 16777216,
  "slow_query_log": true,
  "connect_timeout": 10,
  "log_output": "INSIGHTS",
  "net_read_timeout": 30,
  "innodb_lock_wait_timeout": 50,
  "wait_timeout": 28800,
  "innodb_rollback_on_timeout": true,
  "group_concat_max_len": 1024,
  "net_buffer_length": 16384,
  "innodb_print_all_deadlocks": true,
  "innodb_online_alter_log_max_size": 134217728,
  "interactive_timeout": 3600,
  "innodb_log_buffer_size": 16777216,
  "max_allowed_packet": 67108864,
  "max_heap_table_size": 16777216,
  "innodb_ft_server_stopword_table": "db_name/table_name",
  "innodb_read_io_threads": 10,
  "sql_require_primary_key": true,
  "default_time_zone": "+03:00",
  "long_query_time": 10
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|net_write_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.|
|internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine|string|false|none|The storage engine for in-memory internal temporary tables.|
|sql_mode|string|false|none|Global SQL mode. Set to empty to use MySQL server defaults. When creating a new service and not setting this field Aiven default SQL mode (strict, SQL standard compliant) will be assigned.|
|information_schema_stats_expiry|integer|false|none|The time, in seconds, before cached statistics expire|
|sort_buffer_size|integer|false|none|Sort buffer size in bytes for ORDER BY optimization. Default is 262144 (256K)|
|innodb_thread_concurrency|integer|false|none|Defines the maximum number of threads permitted inside of InnoDB. Default is 0 (infinite concurrency - no limit)|
|innodb_write_io_threads|integer|false|none|The number of I/O threads for write operations in InnoDB. Default is 4. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|innodb_ft_min_token_size|integer|false|none|Minimum length of words that are stored in an InnoDB FULLTEXT index. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|innodb_change_buffer_max_size|integer|false|none|Maximum size for the InnoDB change buffer, as a percentage of the total size of the buffer pool. Default is 25|
|innodb_flush_neighbors|integer|false|none|Specifies whether flushing a page from the InnoDB buffer pool also flushes other dirty pages in the same extent (default is 1): 0 - dirty pages in the same extent are not flushed, 1 - flush contiguous dirty pages in the same extent, 2 - flush dirty pages in the same extent|
|tmp_table_size|integer|false|none|Limits the size of internal in-memory tables. Also set max_heap_table_size. Default is 16777216 (16M)|
|slow_query_log|boolean|false|none|Slow query log enables capturing of slow queries. Setting slow_query_log to false also truncates the mysql.slow_log table. Default is off|
|connect_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with Bad handshake|
|log_output|string|false|none|The slow log output destination when slow_query_log is ON. To enable MySQL AI Insights, choose INSIGHTS. To use MySQL AI Insights and the mysql.slow_log table at the same time, choose INSIGHTS,TABLE. To only use the mysql.slow_log table, choose TABLE. To silence slow logs, choose NONE.|
|net_read_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read.|
|innodb_lock_wait_timeout|integer|false|none|The length of time in seconds an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock before giving up. Default is 120.|
|wait_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds the server waits for activity on a noninteractive connection before closing it.|
|innodb_rollback_on_timeout|boolean|false|none|When enabled a transaction timeout causes InnoDB to abort and roll back the entire transaction. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|group_concat_max_len|integer|false|none|The maximum permitted result length in bytes for the GROUP_CONCAT() function.|
|net_buffer_length|integer|false|none|Start sizes of connection buffer and result buffer. Default is 16384 (16K). Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|innodb_print_all_deadlocks|boolean|false|none|When enabled, information about all deadlocks in InnoDB user transactions is recorded in the error log. Disabled by default.|
|innodb_online_alter_log_max_size|integer|false|none|The upper limit in bytes on the size of the temporary log files used during online DDL operations for InnoDB tables.|
|interactive_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds the server waits for activity on an interactive connection before closing it.|
|innodb_log_buffer_size|integer|false|none|The size in bytes of the buffer that InnoDB uses to write to the log files on disk.|
|max_allowed_packet|integer|false|none|Size of the largest message in bytes that can be received by the server. Default is 67108864 (64M)|
|max_heap_table_size|integer|false|none|Limits the size of internal in-memory tables. Also set tmp_table_size. Default is 16777216 (16M)|
|innodb_ft_server_stopword_table|string \| null|false|none|This option is used to specify your own InnoDB FULLTEXT index stopword list for all InnoDB tables.|
|innodb_read_io_threads|integer|false|none|The number of I/O threads for read operations in InnoDB. Default is 4. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|sql_require_primary_key|boolean|false|none|Require primary key to be defined for new tables or old tables modified with ALTER TABLE and fail if missing. It is recommended to always have primary keys because various functionality may break if any large table is missing them.|
|default_time_zone|string|false|none|Default server time zone as an offset from UTC (from -12:00 to +12:00), a time zone name, or 'SYSTEM' to use the MySQL server default.|
|long_query_time|number|false|none|The slow_query_logs work as SQL statements that take more than long_query_time seconds to execute. Default is 10s|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine|TempTable|
|internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine|MEMORY|
|log_output|INSIGHTS|
|log_output|INSIGHTS,TABLE|
|log_output|NONE|
|log_output|TABLE|

<h2 id="tocS_json-schema-valkey">json-schema-valkey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajson-schema-valkey"></a>
<a id="schema_json-schema-valkey"></a>
<a id="tocSjson-schema-valkey"></a>
<a id="tocsjson-schema-valkey"></a>

```json
{
  "ssl": true,
  "lfu_log_factor": 10,
  "frequent_snapshots": true,
  "maxmemory_policy": "noeviction",
  "io_threads": 1,
  "lfu_decay_time": 1,
  "pubsub_client_output_buffer_limit": 64,
  "active_expire_effort": 1,
  "notify_keyspace_events": "",
  "persistence": "off",
  "timeout": 300,
  "acl_channels_default": "allchannels",
  "number_of_databases": 16
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ssl|boolean|false|none|none|
|lfu_log_factor|integer|false|none|none|
|frequent_snapshots|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Valkey will create frequent local RDB snapshots. When disabled, Valkey will only take RDB snapshots when a backup is created, based on the backup schedule. This setting is ignored when `valkey_persistence` is set to `off`.|
|maxmemory_policy|string \| null|false|none|none|
|io_threads|integer|false|none|Set Valkey IO thread count. Changing this will cause a restart of the Valkey service.|
|lfu_decay_time|integer|false|none|none|
|pubsub_client_output_buffer_limit|integer|false|none|Set output buffer limit for pub / sub clients in MB. The value is the hard limit, the soft limit is 1/4 of the hard limit. When setting the limit, be mindful of the available memory in the selected service plan.|
|active_expire_effort|integer|false|none|Valkey reclaims expired keys both when accessed and in the background. The background process scans for expired keys to free memory. Increasing the active-expire-effort setting (default 1, max 10) uses more CPU to reclaim expired keys faster, reducing memory usage but potentially increasing latency.|
|notify_keyspace_events|string|false|none|none|
|persistence|string|false|none|When persistence is 'rdb', Valkey does RDB dumps each 10 minutes if any key is changed. Also RDB dumps are done according to backup schedule for backup purposes. When persistence is 'off', no RDB dumps and backups are done, so data can be lost at any moment if service is restarted for any reason, or if service is powered off. Also service can't be forked.|
|timeout|integer|false|none|none|
|acl_channels_default|string|false|none|Determines default pub/sub channels' ACL for new users if ACL is not supplied. When this option is not defined, all_channels is assumed to keep backward compatibility. This option doesn't affect Valkey configuration acl-pubsub-default.|
|number_of_databases|integer|false|none|Set number of Valkey databases. Changing this will cause a restart of the Valkey service.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|maxmemory_policy|noeviction|
|maxmemory_policy|allkeys-lru|
|maxmemory_policy|volatile-lru|
|maxmemory_policy|allkeys-random|
|maxmemory_policy|volatile-random|
|maxmemory_policy|volatile-ttl|
|maxmemory_policy|volatile-lfu|
|maxmemory_policy|allkeys-lfu|
|persistence|off|
|persistence|rdb|
|acl_channels_default|allchannels|
|acl_channels_default|resetchannels|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|false|none|Healthcheck mode|

|port|integer(int64)|false|none|Healthcheck port|
|timeout|integer(int64)|false|none|Healthcheck timeout value (default: 2). Must be lower than or equal to Interval|
|retries|integer(int64)|false|none|Number of retries before considering a Service failed|
|tls-sni|string|false|none|SNI domain for HTTPS healthchecks|

|timescaledb-settings|[json-schema-timescaledb](#schemajson-schema-timescaledb)|false|none|TimescaleDB extension configuration values|
|databases|[[dbaas-database-name](#schemadbaas-database-name)]|false|none|List of PostgreSQL databases|
|ip-filter|[string]|false|none|Allowed CIDR address blocks for incoming connections|
|backups|[[dbaas-service-backup](#schemadbaas-service-backup)]|false|none|List of backups for the service|
|termination-protection|boolean|false|none|Service is protected against termination and powering off|
|pgaudit-settings|[json-schema-pgaudit](#schemajson-schema-pgaudit)|false|none|PGAudit settings|
|notifications|[[dbaas-service-notification](#schemadbaas-service-notification)]|false|none|Service notifications|
|components|[object]|false|none|Service component information objects|
|synchronous-replication|[enum-pg-synchronous-replication](#schemaenum-pg-synchronous-replication)|false|none|Synchronous replication type. Note that the service plan also needs to support synchronous replication.|
|pglookout-settings|[json-schema-pglookout](#schemajson-schema-pglookout)|false|none|PGLookout settings|
|maintenance|[dbaas-service-maintenance](#schemadbaas-service-maintenance)|false|none|Automatic maintenance settings|
|disk-size|integer(int64)|false|none|TODO UNIT disk space for data storage|
|node-memory|integer(int64)|false|none|TODO UNIT of memory for each node|
|uri|string|false|none|URI for connecting to the service (may be absent)|
|uri-params|object|false|none|service_uri parameterized into key-value pairs|
|version|string|false|none|PostgreSQL version|
|created-at|string(date-time)|false|none|Service creation timestamp (ISO 8601)|
|plan|string|true|none|Subscription plan|
|work-mem|integer(int64)|false|none|Sets the maximum amount of memory to be used by a query operation (such as a sort or hash table) before writing to temporary disk files, in MB. Default is 1MB + 0.075% of total RAM (up to 32MB).|
|shared-buffers-percentage|integer(int64)|false|none|Percentage of total RAM that the database server uses for shared memory buffers. Valid range is 20-60 (float), which corresponds to 20% - 60%. This setting adjusts the shared_buffers configuration value.|
|pg-settings|[json-schema-pg](#schemajson-schema-pg)|false|none|PostgreSQL-specific settings|
|max-connections|integer(int64)|false|none|Maximum number of connections allowed to an instance|
|users|[object]|false|none|List of service users|

|state|rebuilding|
|state|rebalancing|
|state|poweroff|

<h2 id="tocS_json-schema-kafka-rest">json-schema-kafka-rest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajson-schema-kafka-rest"></a>
<a id="schema_json-schema-kafka-rest"></a>
<a id="tocSjson-schema-kafka-rest"></a>
<a id="tocsjson-schema-kafka-rest"></a>

```json
{
  "producer_compression_type": "gzip",
  "name_strategy_validation": true,
  "name_strategy": "topic_name",
  "consumer_enable_auto_commit": true,
  "producer_acks": "1",
  "consumer_request_max_bytes": 67108864,
  "producer_max_request_size": 1048576,
  "simpleconsumer_pool_size_max": 25,
  "producer_linger_ms": 0,
  "consumer_request_timeout_ms": 1000
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|producer_compression_type|string|false|none|Specify the default compression type for producers. This configuration accepts the standard compression codecs ('gzip', 'snappy', 'lz4', 'zstd'). It additionally accepts 'none' which is the default and equivalent to no compression.|
|name_strategy_validation|boolean|false|none|If true, validate that given schema is registered under expected subject name by the used name strategy when producing messages.|
|name_strategy|string|false|none|Name strategy to use when selecting subject for storing schemas|
|consumer_enable_auto_commit|boolean|false|none|If true the consumer's offset will be periodically committed to Kafka in the background|
|producer_acks|string|false|none|The number of acknowledgments the producer requires the leader to have received before considering a request complete. If set to 'all' or '-1', the leader will wait for the full set of in-sync replicas to acknowledge the record.|
|consumer_request_max_bytes|integer|false|none|Maximum number of bytes in unencoded message keys and values by a single request|
|producer_max_request_size|integer|false|none|The maximum size of a request in bytes. Note that Kafka broker can also cap the record batch size.|
|simpleconsumer_pool_size_max|integer|false|none|Maximum number of SimpleConsumers that can be instantiated per broker|
|producer_linger_ms|integer|false|none|Wait for up to the given delay to allow batching records together|
|consumer_request_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum total time to wait for messages for a request if the maximum number of messages has not yet been reached|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|producer_compression_type|gzip|
|producer_compression_type|snappy|
|producer_compression_type|lz4|
|producer_compression_type|zstd|
|producer_compression_type|none|
|name_strategy|topic_name|
|name_strategy|record_name|
|name_strategy|topic_record_name|
|producer_acks|all|
|producer_acks|-1|
|producer_acks|0|
|producer_acks|1|
|consumer_request_timeout_ms|1000|
|consumer_request_timeout_ms|15000|
|consumer_request_timeout_ms|30000|

```json
  "node-cidr-mask-size-ipv4": 1,
  "node-cidr-mask-size-ipv6": 1
}
```

EXPERIMENTAL: Cluster networking configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster-cidr|string|false|none|CIDR Range for Pods in cluster. This must not overlap with any IP ranges assigned to pods. Max of two, comma-separated, dual-stack CIDRs is allowed.<br>              If not specified, defaults to 192.168.0.0/16.|
|service-cluster-ip-range|string|false|none|CIDR range for service cluster IPs. This must not overlap with any IP ranges assigned to nodes or pods. Max of two, comma-separated, dual-stack CIDRs is allowed. The IPv6 range must be no larger than a /108 (upstream Kubernetes apiserver limit).<br>              If not specified, defaults to 10.96.0.0/12.|
|node-cidr-mask-size-ipv4|integer(int64)|false|none|Mask size for node cidr in cluster. It must be larger than, and at most 16 bits longer than, the Pod CIDR subnet mask. Defaults to 24|
|node-cidr-mask-size-ipv6|integer(int64)|false|none|Mask size for node cidr in cluster. It must be larger than, and at most 16 bits longer than, the Pod CIDR subnet mask. Defaults to 64|

DBaaS plan backup config

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max-count|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Maximum number of backups to keep. Zero when no backups are created.|
|interval|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The interval, in hours, at which backups are generated.<br>                                            For some services, like PostgreSQL, this is the interval<br>                                            at which full snapshots are taken and continuous incremental<br>                                            backup stream is maintained in addition to that.|
|recovery-mode|string|false|read-only|Mechanism how backups can be restored. 'regular'<br>                                            means a backup is restored as is so that the system<br>                                            is restored to the state it was when the backup was generated.<br>                                            'pitr' means point-in-time-recovery, which allows restoring the system to any state since the first available full snapshot.|
|frequent-interval-minutes|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Interval of taking a frequent backup in service types supporting different backup schedules|
|frequent-oldest-age-minutes|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Maximum age of the oldest frequent backup in service types supporting different backup schedules|
|infrequent-interval-minutes|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Interval of taking a frequent backup in service types supporting different backup schedules|
|infrequent-oldest-age-minutes|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Maximum age of the oldest infrequent backup in service types supporting different backup schedules|

|node-count|integer(int64)|false|none|Number of service nodes in the active plan|
|connection-info|object|false|none|Opensearch connection information properties|
|node-cpu-count|integer(int64)|false|none|Number of CPUs for each node|
|prometheus-uri|object|true|none|Prometheus integration URI|
|integrations|[[dbaas-integration](#schemadbaas-integration)]|false|none|Service integrations|
|zone|string|false|none|The zone where the service is running|
|node-states|[[dbaas-node-state](#schemadbaas-node-state)]|false|none|State of individual service nodes|
|name|[dbaas-service-name](#schemadbaas-service-name)|true|none|Service name|
|keep-index-refresh-interval|boolean|false|none|Aiven automation resets index.refresh_interval to default value for every index to be sure that indices are always visible to search. If it doesn't fit your case, you can disable this by setting up this flag to true.|
|type|[dbaas-service-type-name](#schemadbaas-service-type-name)|true|none|Service type code|
|state|[enum-service-state](#schemaenum-service-state)|false|none|State of the service|
|ip-filter|[string]|false|none|Allowed CIDR address blocks for incoming connections|
|backups|[[dbaas-service-backup](#schemadbaas-service-backup)]|false|none|List of backups for the service|
|termination-protection|boolean|false|none|Service is protected against termination and powering off|
|notifications|[[dbaas-service-notification](#schemadbaas-service-notification)]|false|none|Service notifications|
|components|[object]|false|none|Service component information objects|
|index-patterns|[object]|false|none|Allows you to create glob style patterns and set a max number of indexes matching this pattern you want to keep. Creating indexes exceeding this value will cause the oldest one to get deleted. You could for example create a pattern looking like 'logs.?' and then create index logs.1, logs.2 etc, it will delete logs.1 once you create logs.6. Do note 'logs.?' does not apply to logs.10. Note: Setting max_index_count to 0 will do nothing and the pattern gets ignored.|
|maintenance|[dbaas-service-maintenance](#schemadbaas-service-maintenance)|false|none|Automatic maintenance settings|
|index-template|object|false|none|Template settings for all new indexes|
|disk-size|integer(int64)|false|none|TODO UNIT disk space for data storage|
|node-memory|integer(int64)|false|none|TODO UNIT of memory for each node|
|uri|string|false|none|URI for connecting to the service (may be absent)|
|opensearch-settings|[json-schema-opensearch](#schemajson-schema-opensearch)|false|none|OpenSearch-specific settings|
|uri-params|object|false|none|service_uri parameterized into key-value pairs|
|version|string|false|none|OpenSearch version|
|created-at|string(date-time)|false|none|Service creation timestamp (ISO 8601)|
|plan|string|true|none|Subscription plan|
|opensearch-dashboards|object|false|none|OpenSearch Dashboards settings|
|users|[object]|false|none|List of service users|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|running|
|state|rebuilding|
|state|rebalancing|
|state|poweroff|
